name: Agriculture
blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

points.desc: Deere's precision agriculture line (See and Spray, autonomous tractors) is the reference commercial deployment.
points.name: Precision ag is shipping product

points.desc: Census BTOS covers agriculture-adjacent sectors in its fortnightly AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Economic Research Service publishes the data series on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms - variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment. The federal measurement layer.
points.name: USDA ERS measures US adoption

points.desc: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's digital agriculture program, with the 60 Decibels-supported Digital Agriculture Index, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact.
points.name: FAO benchmarks digital agriculture globally

points.desc: The AgriFoodTech investment research tracks venture capital into agricultural AI, robotics, computer vision, and farm-management software - the sector's funding barometer.
points.name: AgFunder indexes the investment flow

points.desc: Planet Labs' high-resolution imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial ML, and EarthDaily's field-level crop indicators supply the AI-ready observation data behind yield prediction and crop-stress detection.
points.name: The satellite layer feeds the models

points.desc: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption across crop and livestock production.
points.name: AEM tracks the machinery standards

points.desc: The nonprofit consortium sets the open data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites - the plumbing under everything else.
points.name: AgGateway makes the data interoperable

points.desc: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is the scientific organization connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice.
points.name: ISPA bridges the science and the field

points.desc: The 100 Million Farmers initiative tracks AI adoption through the lens of climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics globally.
points.name: WEF tracks climate-smart adoption

points.desc: Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the large digital-farming platforms turning soil, weather, and yield data into planting and input prescriptions with machine learning.
points.name: The agribusiness platforms run the prescriptions

points.desc: CNH Industrial's Raven division builds driverless tractor technology, AI path-planning, and precision application - the equipment layer beyond Deere.
points.name: CNH and Raven automate the other fleets

points.desc: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder kills weeds with computer vision and lasers instead of herbicide; Monarch builds electric driverless tractors - narrow AI shipping as farm equipment.
points.name: The pure-plays attack single problems

summary: Precision agriculture - vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, autonomous equipment - is deployed at commercial scale. Who tracks it: federal adoption data, a UN benchmarking framework, a venture index, and standards bodies, layered over the equipment giants and AI pure-plays actually shipping it.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey asks agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting firms (NAICS 11) whether they used AI in the last two weeks, but the latest and prior period shares are both suppressed, so no public adoption rate is available from that series. USDA ERS is the federal measurement layer for precision agriculture adoption, publishing data on variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, and autonomous equipment across US farms. FAO's e-Agriculture program operates as a global community of practice for ICT use in agriculture, forestry, fisheries, and rural development.

On the equipment side, Carbon Robotics sells the LaserWeeder and Carbon Autonomy, using computer vision and lasers to eliminate weeds, reduce costs, increase yields, and improve sustainability; its Carbon AI is powered by a Large Plant Model trained on data collected by LaserWeeders worldwide. John Deere's precision agriculture line, including See and Spray and autonomous tractors, is presented as the reference commercial deployment. Raven, a brand of CNH, provides automated and autonomous farm technologies for precision application and path planning, with the stated goal of maximizing yield with less resources. Planet Labs supplies daily satellite imagery and Earth data analytics for agricultural monitoring, feeding the observation layer behind yield prediction and crop stress detection.

The agribusiness platform layer turns that data into prescriptions. Climate FieldView reports that farmers using its seed scripts saw an average increase of +5 bu/ac compared to users who wrote their own scripts, and its FieldView Drive 2.0 can send seed scripts without a thumb drive, has built-in GPS, and offers faster data syncing and compatibility with a wider range of equipment. AgGateway provides the interoperability plumbing, with a North American traceability initiative covering seeding and provenance, including grain traceability, and a European special interest group on farm and crop field identification using standard identifiers.

Investment is selective. Per AgFunder, global agrifoodtech funding hit $16.2 billion in 2025, almost flat versus the prior year at -3%, with investors directing capital toward companies with tangible science, real unit economics, and clear paths to revenue. In 2024 global funding reached $16 billion, a 4% drop from 2023. Asia-Pacific startups raised $4.2 billion as of the end of October 2024, a 38% increase on the $3.1 billion raised over the same period in 2023. African agrifoodtech raised $145 million in the first half of 2024, a 1.6% year-over-year increase, but still just 1.6% of global investment, after a 2023 decline of 62% to $275 million. AgFunder also notes developing markets agrifoodtech funding grew 63% between 2023 and 2024, versus a 4% decline globally.

On standards and policy, AgGateway says its traceability work contributes to food safety and regulatory compliance. AEM brings agricultural equipment manufacturers together to shape policy, understand data, and develop strategies for environmental, political, and economic changes. ISPA connects academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice and maintains a precision agriculture definition in over fifteen languages. For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the picture is one of shipping commercial products and vendor-reported yield gains, but the official Census AI-use share is suppressed, so measured adoption at the sector level remains a gap in the public data.

https://www.aem.org/.brief: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers (AEM) describes itself as a North American organization for construction and agriculture equipment makers operating globally. According to the organization, its main areas of work include policy advocacy, safety, trade shows and events, and market data. AEM states that it brings agricultural original equipment manufacturers together to influence policy, interpret data, and plan for environmental, political, and economic shifts. For construction, the association says it helps manufacturers influence policy, use data, and respond to changing customer demands. The page also notes that AEM will hold its Market Share Statistics Fall Meetings & Forum on September 22, 24, 2026, at its Milwaukee headquarters.

https://www.ispag.org/.brief: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is a scientific organization that develops technologies to help feed the world and improve quality of life. It offers a definition of precision agriculture in more than fifteen languages and gives members access to directories, networking, and discounted conference registration. Members receive a monthly “ISPA newsletter” that shares news, job listings, and event information, and the society is preparing for the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP in summer 2026. Country Representatives promote ISPA worldwide; applicants must email info@ispag.org with a bio, CV, and be current members, and members can post job announcements on the site and in newsletters.

https://www.planet.com/.brief: Planet Labs offers a platform called Planet Insights that brings together daily satellite imagery, derived data products, and cloud-based tools in one place. The company claims its imagery is the highest-frequency commercial Earth observation data, enabling daily monitoring, high-resolution tasking, and deeper derived insights. It says the platform lets users view the planet in time, space, and frequency, helping them make decisions quickly and confidently. Planet reports that organizations across many sectors use the platform to address operational challenges with a global, dynamic perspective.

https://www.ers.usda.gov/.brief: The USDA Economic Research Service page describes several data resources it offers. It states that State Fact Sheets provide information on population, income, poverty, food security, education, employment, farm characteristics, financial indicators, top commodities, and agricultural exports for all states, with metro/nonmetro breakouts and county-level links where available. The page also notes that the Food Price Outlook supplies food price data and forecasts changes in the Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index for food. Additionally, it lists a Vegetables and Pulses Data collection covering statistics on fresh and processed vegetables and dry pulses in the United States, along with some global data. The page mentions an email notification service for announcements of reports and news.

https://agfunder.com/research/.brief: AgFunder reports that global agrifoodtech funding reached $16.2 billion in 2025, down 3% year-over-year, with investors becoming more selective and favoring companies demonstrating "tangible science, real unit economics, and clear paths to revenue." While overall funding remained relatively flat, regional patterns diverged significantly: developing markets agrifoodtech grew 63% between 2023 and 2024, Asia-Pacific startups raised $4.2 billion as of October 2024 (a 38% increase), and African agrifoodtech showed mild recovery with $145 million raised in the first half of 2024 after a 62% decline in 2023. These trends suggest a sector undergoing consolidation, with capital concentrating in regions and companies meeting stricter investment criteria.

https://www.fao.org/digital-agriculture/.brief: The page presents e-Agriculture as a worldwide community for dialogue and information sharing about information and communication technologies in sustainable agriculture and rural development. It says the initiative grew out of the World Summit on the Information Society’s Action Line C7, and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations was assigned to facilitate it. The page also reports that the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 chose 13 youth-led solutions from 137 valid applications to take part in a final pitch event in China. It notes that three winners were announced at the final pitch in Hangzhou on 10 September 2026, including AgriKonnekt from Kenya and Berikanpreneur from Indonesia.
